title: Non-overlapping Intervals
prompt:
Return the minimum number of intervals to remove so the rest don't overlap.

**Example**: `[[1,2],[2,3],[3,4],[1,3]]` → `1` (remove `[1,3]`).

Greedy: sort by END, always keep the interval that finishes earliest — it leaves the most room for the rest.
hints: Sort by end value. Keep a running `prevEnd`.
If an interval starts at or after prevEnd, keep it (update prevEnd); otherwise it overlaps → count a removal.
Keeping the earliest-ending interval is the greedy choice that maximizes survivors.

solution.explanation: This is the classic activity-selection greedy: sorting by finish time and always keeping the earliest-finishing compatible interval provably retains the maximum number, so the removals counted are minimal. O(n log n).
